_owner: Pranav. These are the on-screen actions Remy can trigger. Ahmed's live.js turns each into a screen event (docs/CONTRACT.md).

tools.name: find_recipe
tools.description: Call once when the cook names or changes the dish, before giving recipe-specific guidance. Pass the cook's own words. Use the returned hand-checked recipe if one exists; otherwise follow the result and call create_recipe. Do not call repeatedly for the same dish.

dish.description: The dish in the cook's words.

tools.name: create_recipe
tools.description: Create and show a recipe only after find_recipe returns no hand-checked match, or when the cook asks to adapt a recipe. Keep it short and home-cook friendly. Include visible looks_right and looks_wrong cues and an objective done_when for every step. Never invent timer durations or food-safety temperatures: the server checks and replaces those values, so use its returned recipe.

timer.description: Only if this step is timed.

tools.name: show_tip
tools.description: Show and say one short, immediately useful instruction. Use info for requested or timely guidance, warning for a likely non-dangerous mistake, and urgent only for time-sensitive correction that is not a safety emergency. Visible smoke from a hot pan, even heavy smoke, gets one plain heat-down tip, never a roast or safety_alert for smoke alone. Ask one concrete question instead when the view is uncertain. Do not call when everything is fine, repeat an unchanged tip, or bundle multiple tips. Use safety_alert for immediate danger such as visible flames.

tools.name: roast
tools.description: Use only after a non-safety mistake is clearly visible or the cook confirms it. Give the corrective action first, then one short line in the current mode. Target the food or technique, never the person. Smoke alone is not a roastable mistake or proof that food is burnt. Level 1 is the first incident; increase only for a separate confirmed repeat, never more frames of the same incident. Do not call when uncertain, during unresolved danger, for normal waiting, or for an unchanged mistake already roasted.

level.description: 1 = first confirmed incident, 2 = separate repeat, 3 = third separate repeat.

mistake.description: Exact key from roasts.json: burning, overcooked, undercooked, raw, too_much_salt, messy_station, wrong_order, or slow.

tools.name: safety_alert
tools.description: Highest-priority red warning for clearly visible or cook-confirmed immediate danger such as flames or fire, fingers in a knife's path, raw-meat cross-contamination, or a child or pet beside an active hob. Smoke from a hot pan, even heavy smoke, is a show_tip to turn down heat, not a safety_alert unless flames or fire are visible. Call this before every other action, use a direct imperative, and drop all comedy. Do not pair it with roast while danger remains. Do not use for ordinary cooking mistakes or an ambiguous view; ask first if it is safe to wait for an answer.

text.description: Short and clear, e.g. 'Flames in the pan: turn off the heat and cover it'.

tools.name: update_step
tools.description: Advance only when the current recipe step's done_when is visibly satisfied or the cook confirms it. Never infer completion from elapsed time alone. Set current_step to the 0-based step the cook is now on, say one short next instruction, and do not repeat the same update.

current_step.description: 0-based index of the step the cook is now on.

tools.name: start_timer
tools.description: Start exactly one countdown when you see or hear that the timed activity has begun, such as pasta entering the water. Use minutes only from the active recipe timer or cook-times table; never guess or silently choose within a range. If timing or start is unclear, ask. Do not start a duplicate. Say the label and duration once so the cook can correct it.

check_at_minutes.description: When to check/taste, e.g. 1 minute before the end.

tools.name: cancel_timer
tools.description: Cancel only when the cook asks, confirms the timer is wrong, or the timed activity has definitely stopped and the countdown no longer applies. Use the exact active timer id, say what was cancelled, and never cancel merely because the camera view changed.
